::: {.lead-note}

I have worked in Indonesian public procurement since 2015 — first inside
government as a procurement official, commitment-making official, and member of
provincial selection working groups, and since 2018 as a nationally certified
facilitator, competency assessor, and advisor. My work sits at the point where
procurement rules meet procurement practice: how buying decisions are actually
planned, how contracts are actually managed, and how procurement officials
actually acquire competence.

:::

::: {.note}

This page describes my professional practice. It is distinct from my
[academic research](../research.qmd), which is in development, urban, and
spatial economics. Where the two meet — empirical work on competition and
efficiency in Indonesian government procurement — the papers appear under
Research.

:::

## Areas of expertise

:::: {.grid-2}


::: {.area}

#### Procurement Planning & Strategy
Translating programme objectives into a procurement approach: packaging, market
approach, contract type, and timing. Most procurement failures are decided
before the tender opens.

:::

::: {.area}

#### Specification & Cost Estimation
Specifications that describe a need rather than a product, and cost estimates
that survive scrutiny — the two documents that most often determine whether a
competitive process is possible at all.

:::

::: {.area}

#### Supplier Selection
Evaluation design, qualification, and the trade-off between price and value.
Selection method is a policy choice, not an administrative formality.

:::

::: {.area}

#### Contract Management
Performance monitoring, variation and claim handling, acceptance, and dispute
resolution — including construction and consultancy contracts.

:::

::: {.area}

#### Competency Development
Design and delivery of training and competency assessment across the levels of
Indonesia's public procurement competency framework, from foundation through
advanced practice.

:::

::: {.area}

#### Procurement Governance & Policy
Institutional procurement guidelines, probity advice, and drafting of
organisational procurement regulations for public bodies.

:::
